cards.title: Proper unlabeled compression of ample classes
cards.formal: Does every nonempty ample concept class C⊆{0,1}ᵁ on a finite domain U admit a proper unlabeled sample compression scheme of size at most d=VC(C)? Precisely, do there exist maps κ:RS(C)→{A⊆U:|A|≤d} and ρ:{A⊆U:|A|≤d}→C such that, for every realizable labeled partial sample s, κ(s)⊆dom(s) and ρ(κ(s)) agrees with every label in s? The stored object is only an unordered subset of the sample’s input points. The bound is d, not an unspecified multiple of d.
cards.why: Would extend sharp label-free sample compression from maximum classes to the larger class characterized by equality of shattering and strong shattering, clarifying how far the VC dimension controls lossless reconstruction of consistent samples.
cards.status_note: Read the full proper-compression definition and the distinction between maximum and ample classes, then checked the 2024 oriented-matroid theorem and its explicit remaining-question paragraph. Also checked the revised labeled-compression work for complexes of oriented matroids, whose retained labels make its result different. Searches through 12 September 2026 found no resolution for every finite ample class; searches are not exhaustive.

importance.reason: A sharp structural extension of sample compression, connecting VC dimension with reconstruction from unlabeled points for a broad class beyond maximum systems. Existing score retained.

sentences: An ample class strongly shatters every set of coordinates that it shatters.
A compressor selects at most d input points from any realizable labeled sample, where d is the class’s VC dimension.
A reconstructor must recover a concept in the original class consistent with all sample labels while receiving only the selected points.
Maximum classes satisfy this exact bound, and labeled compression is known more generally.
The 2024 oriented-matroid results still leave proper unlabeled size-d compression for all ample classes open.

cards.definitions: A concept c∈C is a function c:U→{0,1}. A set A⊆U is shattered by C if {c|_A:c∈C}={0,1}ᴬ. It is strongly shattered if some b:U∖A→{0,1} has the property that, for every a:A→{0,1}, the combined labeling a∪b belongs to C. Thus strong shattering requires a full cube of concepts with identical labels outside A. The class is ample when every shattered set is strongly shattered; ample classes are also called lopsided or shattering-extremal. Its VC dimension d is the maximum size of a shattered set. A labeled partial sample is a function s:A→{0,1} on some A⊆U, equivalently a set of pairs (x,s(x)) with distinct x. It is realizable if s=c|_A for some c∈C; RS(C) contains every such sample, including the empty sample. The compressor κ sees the entire labeled sample and may use its labels to choose a subset κ(s) of its domain, of size at most d. It sends only that subset. The reconstructor ρ receives no labels, ordering, multiplicities, sample size, omitted sample points or auxiliary bits; U,C,κ and ρ are fixed and shared beforehand. It returns a total concept belonging to C, which must agree with the original entire sample, including omitted labels. This is the proper convention explicitly used in the full source. Requiring ρ on all subsets of size at most d is equivalent to defining it only on Im(κ), because C is nonempty and unused inputs can be assigned any fixed concept. The existence of κ,ρ is quantified separately for each finite C; no running-time bound for constructing or evaluating them, distributional assumption or probability of error is part of the statement. For d=0 a nonempty class has a single concept and the empty compressed set suffices. A maximum class of dimension d has cardinality Σ_{j=0}^d binomial(|U|,j); every maximum class is ample, but the converse need not hold.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove existence of the two maps with the stated d-point bound for every finite nonempty ample class, or give an ample class with a proof that no such pair of maps exists. A scheme retaining labels, returning a hypothesis outside C, storing extra information, or exceeding d points does not meet the target. A scheme that handles only full concepts rather than every realizable partial sample is also insufficient. Failure of a proposed corner-peeling construction alone does not refute existence of a compression scheme.

cards.context:
The source constructs proper unlabeled schemes of size d for maximum classes. Its open extension concerns all ample classes, a strictly larger family.

Size-d labeled compression is already known for ample classes. The new requirement is that the reconstructor recover a consistent concept from selected input points after all their labels have been removed.

The source exhibits a maximum class of VC dimension three without a corner, refuting earlier corner-peeling arguments. It nevertheless proves the compression theorem for maximum classes. The absence of corners therefore does not imply the desired maps do not exist.

The 2024 paper proves proper unlabeled schemes for oriented matroids and for complexes of oriented matroids admitting corner peelings. It explicitly states that the general ample-class question remains open.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. We aim for benchmarks of 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. All three use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The possible 1,000-problem expansion has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The targets are 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. Top 100, Top 500 and the possible Top 1000 use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
